# Introduction
We will demonstrate how to use ctSVG to identify cell-type-specific SVGs with cell type annotations from Xenium data. The Xenium dataset of a human lung cancer sample was downloaded from the [10x website](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/preview-data-ffpe-human-lung-cancer-with-xenium-multimodal-cell-segmentation-1-standard).

# Load package
```{r setup}
library(ctSVG)
mydir <- "~/Desktop/Research/ctSVG/xenium_human_lungcancer"
list.files(mydir)
expr <- readRDS(file.path(mydir, "expr.rds"))
coord <- readRDS(file.path(mydir, "coord.rds"))
sc <- readRDS(file.path(mydir, "sc.rds"))
str(expr)
str(coord)
str(sc)
sc <- sc[sc %in% levels(sc)[1:3]]
sc <- droplevels(sc)
```

# Identify spatially variable genes within each cell cluster
```{r}
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
  clutestRes <- ctsvg_test(expr = expr, coord = coord, sc = sc)
))
head(clutestRes)
```

# Fit spatial gene expression patterns within each cell cluster
```{r}
clufitRes <- ctsvg_fit(expr = expr, coord = coord, sc = sc)
```

# Visualize spatial patterns of a single gene
```{r}
plotGene(expr = expr, clufitRes = clufitRes, coord = coord, sc = sc,
         gene = clutestRes$gene[1], cellclu = "0", background = TRUE)
```

# Identify gene modules within each cell cluster
```{r}
moduleRes <- ctsvg_module(clutestRes = clutestRes, clufitRes = clufitRes, sc = sc)
```

# Visualize spatial patterns of metagenes within a cell cluster
```{r}
plotMetagene(clufitRes = clufitRes, coord = coord, sc = sc,
             moduleRes = moduleRes, cellclu = "0", background = TRUE)
```
